claim: HIV-1 is a lentivirus that causes acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS).
source: The human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) is a lentivirus that causes acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about HIV-1 classification and disease causation.

claim: HIV-1 has a small genome encoding the main structural proteins Gag, Pol and Env, the regulatory proteins Tat and Rev, and the accessory proteins Nef, Vif, Vpr, and Vpu.
source: HIV-1 has a small genome encoding the main structural proteins Gag, Pol and Env, the regulatory proteins Tat and Rev, and the accessory proteins Nef, Vif, Vpr, and Vpu (Frankel and Young, 1998).
evidence: Supported by citation to Frankel and Young, 1998.

claim: During viral maturation, Pol is proteolytically cleaved to generate three proteins with enzymatic activity: the viral protease, integrase, and reverse transcriptase.
source: During viral maturation, Pol is proteolytically cleaved to generate three proteins with enzymatic activity: the viral protease, integrase, and reverse transcriptase.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HIV-1 viral maturation.

claim: The viral protease, integrase, and reverse transcriptase are the main targets for chemotherapeutic agents currently in use for the prevention and treatment of AIDS.
source: These enzymes are the main targets for chemotherapeutic agents currently in use for the prevention and treatment of AIDS.
evidence: This is established knowledge about current AIDS treatment strategies.

claim: Combination therapies with these agents have dramatically reduced HIV-1 transmission as well as HIV-1-associated morbidity and mortality.
source: Combination therapies with these agents have dramatically reduced HIV-1 transmission as well as HIV-1-associated morbidity and mortality.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the effectiveness of combination antiretroviral therapy.

claim: Nef is not essential for infection in cell culture.
source: Although not essential for infection in cell culture, Nef enhances viral replication and disease progression in vivo.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Nef function in different contexts.

claim: Nef enhances viral replication and disease progression in vivo.
source: Although not essential for infection in cell culture, Nef enhances viral replication and disease progression in vivo.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Nef function in vivo.

claim: Patients infected with Nef-deficient strains of HIV-1 often do not develop AIDS for over 10 years even if untreated.
source: The pathogenic effects of Nef are underscored by the observation that patients infected with Nef-deficient strains of HIV-1 often do not develop AIDS for over 10 years even if untreated (these patients are referred to as 'long-term non-progressors' or 'slow progressors') (Deacon et al., 1995; Kirchhoff et al., 1995; Gorry et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to Deacon et al., 1995; Kirchhoff et al., 1995; Gorry et al., 2007.

claim: Nef has no enzymatic activity.
source: To date, however, this potential has not been realized mainly because Nef has no enzymatic activity and its mechanisms of action are insufficiently understood.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Nef's biochemical properties.

claim: The best characterized and most critical function of Nef for pathogenesis is the downregulation of CD4 from the surface of infected cells.
source: At the cellular level, Nef has been ascribed multiple functions, of which the best characterized and most critical for pathogenesis is the downregulation of CD4 from the surface of infected cells (Guy et al., 1987; Garcia and Miller, 1991; Carl et al., 2000; Glushakova et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citations to Guy et al., 1987; Garcia and Miller, 1991; Carl et al., 2000; Glushakova et al., 2001.

claim: CD4 is a transmembrane protein that acts as a co-receptor in both the host's immune response and the initial binding of HIV-1 to their target cells.
source: CD4 is a transmembrane protein that acts as a co-receptor in both the host's immune response and the initial binding of HIV-1 to their target cells (Bowers et al., 1997).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bowers et al., 1997.

claim: Nef-induced CD4 downregulation interferes with the immune system.
source: Nef-induced CD4 downregulation interferes with the immune system (Skowronski et al., 1993), prevents superinfection (Benson et al., 1993) and promotes virion release (Lama et al., 1999; Ross et al., 1999), all of which contribute to enhanced HIV-1 propagation.
evidence: Supported by citation to Skowronski et al., 1993.

claim: Nef-induced CD4 downregulation prevents superinfection.
source: Nef-induced CD4 downregulation interferes with the immune system (Skowronski et al., 1993), prevents superinfection (Benson et al., 1993) and promotes virion release (Lama et al., 1999; Ross et al., 1999), all of which contribute to enhanced HIV-1 propagation.
evidence: Supported by citation to Benson et al., 1993.

claim: Nef-induced CD4 downregulation promotes virion release.
source: Nef-induced CD4 downregulation interferes with the immune system (Skowronski et al., 1993), prevents superinfection (Benson et al., 1993) and promotes virion release (Lama et al., 1999; Ross et al., 1999), all of which contribute to enhanced HIV-1 propagation.
evidence: Supported by citations to Lama et al., 1999; Ross et al., 1999.

claim: HIV-1 Nef is a small, polymorphic protein of 200–215 amino acids having a myristoylated N-terminus.
source: HIV-1 Nef is a small, polymorphic protein of 200–215 amino acids having a myristoylated N-terminus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Nef structure.

claim: Nef has a folded core (residues 55–65 and 84–203), with flexible N-terminal (residues 1–54) and C-terminal (residues 204–206) segments, and a central flexible loop (residues 149–179).
source: X-ray crystallography (Lee et al., 1996; Arold et al., 1997; Horenkamp et al., 2011; Jia et al., 2012) and NMR (Grzesiek et al., 1996a, 1997) have shown that Nef has a folded core (residues 55–65 and 84–203), with flexible N-terminal (residues 1–54) and C-terminal (residues 204–206) segments, and a central flexible loop (residues 149–179) (residue numbers correspond to the NL4-3 strain of HIV-1).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lee et al., 1996; Arold et al., 1997; Horenkamp et al., 2011; Jia et al., 2012; Grzesiek et al., 1996a, 1997.

claim: CD4 downregulation depends on Nef myristoylation.
source: CD4 downregulation depends on both Nef myristoylation (Aiken et al., 1994) and specific residues in the loop, including Leu164 and Leu165 (Bresnahan et al., 1998; Craig et al., 1998; Greenberg et al., 1998; Janvier et al., 2003), which are in a sequence context fitting the [DE]XXXL[LI] motif for dileucine-based sorting signals (Bonifacino and Traub, 2003), and the diacidic motif, Asp174-Asp175 (Aiken et al., 1996; Lindwasser et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Aiken et al., 1994.

claim: CD4 downregulation depends on specific residues in the Nef loop, including Leu164 and Leu165.
source: CD4 downregulation depends on both Nef myristoylation (Aiken et al., 1994) and specific residues in the loop, including Leu164 and Leu165 (Bresnahan et al., 1998; Craig et al., 1998; Greenberg et al., 1998; Janvier et al., 2003), which are in a sequence context fitting the [DE]XXXL[LI] motif for dileucine-based sorting signals (Bonifacino and Traub, 2003), and the diacidic motif, Asp174-Asp175 (Aiken et al., 1996; Lindwasser et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bresnahan et al., 1998; Craig et al., 1998; Greenberg et al., 1998; Janvier et al., 2003.

claim: Nef Leu164 and Leu165 are in a sequence context fitting the [DE]XXXL[LI] motif for dileucine-based sorting signals.
source: CD4 downregulation depends on both Nef myristoylation (Aiken et al., 1994) and specific residues in the loop, including Leu164 and Leu165 (Bresnahan et al., 1998; Craig et al., 1998; Greenberg et al., 1998; Janvier et al., 2003), which are in a sequence context fitting the [DE]XXXL[LI] motif for dileucine-based sorting signals (Bonifacino and Traub, 2003), and the diacidic motif, Asp174-Asp175 (Aiken et al., 1996; Lindwasser et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bonifacino and Traub, 2003.

claim: CD4 downregulation depends on the diacidic motif Asp174-Asp175 in Nef.
source: CD4 downregulation depends on both Nef myristoylation (Aiken et al., 1994) and specific residues in the loop, including Leu164 and Leu165 (Bresnahan et al., 1998; Craig et al., 1998; Greenberg et al., 1998; Janvier et al., 2003), which are in a sequence context fitting the [DE]XXXL[LI] motif for dileucine-based sorting signals (Bonifacino and Traub, 2003), and the diacidic motif, Asp174-Asp175 (Aiken et al., 1996; Lindwasser et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Aiken et al., 1996; Lindwasser et al., 2008.

claim: Myristoylation allows recruitment of Nef from the cytosol to the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane.
source: Myristoylation allows recruitment of Nef from the cytosol to the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane (Yu and Felsted, 1992) while the loop engages the clathrin-associated adaptor protein 2 (AP-2) complex (Jin et al., 2005; Chaudhuri et al., 2007; Doray et al., 2007; Lindwasser et al., 2008; Mattera et al., 2011; Jin et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yu and Felsted, 1992.

claim: The Nef loop engages the clathrin-associated adaptor protein 2 (AP-2) complex.
source: Myristoylation allows recruitment of Nef from the cytosol to the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane (Yu and Felsted, 1992) while the loop engages the clathrin-associated adaptor protein 2 (AP-2) complex (Jin et al., 2005; Chaudhuri et al., 2007; Doray et al., 2007; Lindwasser et al., 2008; Mattera et al., 2011; Jin et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jin et al., 2005; Chaudhuri et al., 2007; Doray et al., 2007; Lindwasser et al., 2008; Mattera et al., 2011; Jin et al., 2013.

claim: The Nef:AP-2 complex interacts with the cytosolic tail of CD4, leading to the cooperative assembly of a tripartite Nef:AP-2:CD4 complex.
source: The Nef:AP-2 complex interacts with the cytosolic tail of CD4, leading to the cooperative assembly of a tripartite Nef:AP-2:CD4 complex (Chaudhuri et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chaudhuri et al., 2009.

claim: The Nef:AP-2:CD4 complex nucleates the formation of clathrin-coated pits.
source: This complex nucleates the formation of clathrin-coated pits (Foti et al., 1997; Greenberg et al., 1997; Burtey et al., 2007) that mediate rapid internalization of CD4, followed by its delivery to lysosomes via the multivesicular body pathway (Aiken et al., 1994; Rhee and Marsh, 1994; daSilva et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Foti et al., 1997; Greenberg et al., 1997; Burtey et al., 2007.

claim: Clathrin-coated pits mediate rapid internalization of CD4, followed by its delivery to lysosomes via the multivesicular body pathway.
source: This complex nucleates the formation of clathrin-coated pits (Foti et al., 1997; Greenberg et al., 1997; Burtey et al., 2007) that mediate rapid internalization of CD4, followed by its delivery to lysosomes via the multivesicular body pathway (Aiken et al., 1994; Rhee and Marsh, 1994; daSilva et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Aiken et al., 1994; Rhee and Marsh, 1994; daSilva et al., 2009.

claim: Binding of Nef to AP-2 is direct and dependent on the dileucine and diacidic motifs, and other residues, in the Nef loop.
source: Biochemical analyses have demonstrated that binding of Nef to AP-2 is direct and dependent on the dileucine and diacidic motifs, and other residues, in the Nef loop (Chaudhuri et al., 2007; Doray et al., 2007; Lindwasser et al., 2008; Chaudhuri et al., 2009; Mattera et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chaudhuri et al., 2007; Doray et al., 2007; Lindwasser et al., 2008; Chaudhuri et al., 2009; Mattera et al., 2011.

claim: AP-2 is a heterotetramer composed of α, β2, μ2 and σ2 subunits.
source: AP-2 is a heterotetramer composed of α, β2, μ2 and σ2 subunits.
evidence: This is established knowledge about AP-2 structure.

claim: The N-terminal 'trunk' domains of α and β2 together with the whole μ2 and σ2 subunits constitute the core of the AP-2 complex.
source: The N-terminal 'trunk' domains of α and β2 together with the whole μ2 and σ2 subunits constitute the core of the complex, whereas the C-terminal 'hinge' and 'ear' domains of α and β2 form long projections that extend from the core (Owen et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Owen et al., 2004.

claim: The C-terminal 'hinge' and 'ear' domains of α and β2 form long projections that extend from the AP-2 core.
source: The N-terminal 'trunk' domains of α and β2 together with the whole μ2 and σ2 subunits constitute the core of the complex, whereas the C-terminal 'hinge' and 'ear' domains of α and β2 form long projections that extend from the core (Owen et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Owen et al., 2004.

claim: The AP-2 core undergoes a large conformation change from a 'locked' to an 'open' conformation that allows it to bind sorting signals and to be recruited to membranes via interaction with the phosphatidylinositol lipid PI(4,5)P2.
source: The AP-2 core undergoes a large conformation change from a 'locked' to an 'open' conformation that allows it to bind sorting signals and to be recruited to membranes via interaction with the phosphatidylinositol lipid PI(4,5)P2 (Jackson et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Jackson et al., 2010.

claim: Nef binds to the α–σ2 'hemicomplex' of AP-2.
source: Nef has been shown to bind to the α–σ2 'hemicomplex' (Chaudhuri et al., 2007; Doray et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to Chaudhuri et al., 2007; Doray et al., 2007.

claim: The σ2 subunit (with a small contribution from the α subunit) harbors a binding site for [DE]XXXL[LI]-type signals from host cell proteins.
source: The σ2 subunit (with a small contribution from the α subunit), harbors a binding site for [DE]XXXL[LI]-type signals from host cell proteins (Kelly et al., 2008; Jackson et al., 2010; Mattera et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kelly et al., 2008; Jackson et al., 2010; Mattera et al., 2011.

claim: The σ2 binding site for [DE]XXXL[LI]-type signals is required for Nef binding, most likely through recognition of the Nef dileucine motif.
source: Mutational analyses have shown that this site is also required for Nef binding, most likely through recognition of the Nef dileucine motif (Mattera et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Mattera et al., 2011.

claim: The α subunit has an additional site, comprising Lys298 and Arg341, which is required for Nef binding and CD4 downregulation.
source: The α subunit has an additional site, comprising Lys298 and Arg341, which is also required for Nef binding and CD4 downregulation (Chaudhuri et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chaudhuri et al., 2009.

claim: The second Nef-binding site on α (Lys298 and Arg341) is not known to participate in any host cell function.
source: Importantly, this second site on α is not known to participate in any host cell function, making it a possible target for selective interference.
evidence: This is a statement about the lack of known host cell function for this site.

claim: The crystal structure of Nef (residues 54–203) in complex with the α (residues 1–396) and σ2 (full-length) subunits of AP-2 was solved at 2.9 Å resolution.
source: To elucidate the structural basis for this interaction, we have solved the crystal structure at 2.9 Å resolution of Nef (residues 54–203) in complex with the α (residues 1–396) and σ2 (full-length) subunits of AP-2.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental work reported in this manuscript.

claim: The entire central loop of Nef is well ordered in the crystal structure.
source: The structure reveals that the entire central loop is well ordered, and that most of it contacts the α−σ2 hemicomplex.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the crystal structure.

claim: Most of the Nef central loop contacts the α−σ2 hemicomplex.
source: The structure reveals that the entire central loop is well ordered, and that most of it contacts the α−σ2 hemicomplex.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the crystal structure.

claim: The Nef core is directly involved in contacts with AP-2.
source: The Nef core is directly involved in contacts as well as serves as a scaffold to position the central loop.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the crystal structure.

claim: The Nef core serves as a scaffold to position the central loop.
source: The Nef core is directly involved in contacts as well as serves as a scaffold to position the central loop.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the crystal structure.

claim: The α1–396 form of the AP-2 α–σ2 hemicomplex bound to HIV-1 NL4-3 Nef (54–203) with Kd = 1.8 μM and 1:1 stoichiometry, as determined by isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC).
source: This construct bound to the HIV-1 NL4-3 Nef (54–203) (hereafter, 'Nef') with Kd = 1.8 μM and 1:1 stoichiometry, as determined by isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from ITC experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The asymmetric unit of the crystal contains four Nef:α–σ2 complexes, all in similar conformations.
source: The asymmetric unit contains four Nef:α–σ2 complexes, all in similar conformations, with small variations in the quality of the electron density.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: Nef buries 1170 Å2 in the interface with AP-2.
source: Nef buries 1170 Å2 in this interface, of which two-thirds is buried against σ2 and the remainder against α.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: Two-thirds of the Nef-AP-2 interface is buried against σ2 and the remainder against α.
source: Nef buries 1170 Å2 in this interface, of which two-thirds is buried against σ2 and the remainder against α.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: The α–σ2 unit is essentially rigid, in a conformation identical to that seen in other structures of the AP-2 complex.
source: The α–σ2 unit is essentially rigid, in a conformation identical to that seen in other structures of the AP-2 complex (Collins et al., 2002; Kelly et al., 2008; Jackson et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis, supported by comparison to previous structures.

claim: The Nef core (excluding the central loop 149–179) contains five α-helices (H2, H3, H6, H7, H8) and a five-stranded β-sheet.
source: The Nef core (excluding the central loop 149–179) contains the five α-helices (H2, H3, H6, H7, H8) and five-stranded β-sheet visualized in other Nef crystal structures (Lee et al., 1996; Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure, consistent with previous structures.

claim: The Nef core manifests a poorly ordered N-terminal helix (H1) spanning residues 55–65.
source: The core also manifests a poorly ordered N-terminal helix (H1) spanning residues 55–65, which was not visualized in all of the chains.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: Nef helix H1 (residues 55–65) contains the primary binding site for CD4.
source: This helix was first identified by solution NMR and contains the primary binding site for CD4 (Grzesiek et al., 1996a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Grzesiek et al., 1996a.

claim: The central loop from residues 149–179 was visualized in its entirety in the crystal structure.
source: In contrast to most other crystal structures, the central loop from residues 149–179 was visualized in its entirety (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the crystal structure, shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The central loop of Nef contains two additional helices, one from residues 150–157 (H4), and the other a single turn from 167–170 (H5).
source: The central loop contains two additional helices, one from residues 150–157 (H4), and the other a single turn from 167–170 (H5).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: The central loop of Nef interacts extensively both with the α and σ2 subunits.
source: The central loop interacts extensively both with the α and σ2 subunits (Figure 2D), with the greatest contact surface involving σ2.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the crystal structure, shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The greatest contact surface of the Nef central loop involves σ2.
source: The central loop interacts extensively both with the α and σ2 subunits (Figure 2D), with the greatest contact surface involving σ2.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the crystal structure.

claim: The Nef core interacts primarily via a network of interactions between helix H3 and the α subunit.
source: The core interacts primarily via a network of interactions between helix H3 and the α subunit.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: The Leu164-Leu165 pair of the dileucine motif anchors the loop in a pocket on σ2 just as seen for a dileucine peptide bound to the unlatched AP-2 tetramer.
source: The Leu164-Leu165 pair of the dileucine motif anchors the loop in a pocket on σ2 just as seen for a dileucine peptide bound to the unlatched AP-2 tetramer (Kelly et al., 2008; Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure, compared to a previous structure from Kelly et al., 2008, shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The pocket walls for the dileucine binding site on σ2 are formed by hydrophobic residues.
source: The pocket walls are formed by hydrophobic residues of σ2.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: Nef Glu160 of the motif binds to basic residues on both σ2 and α.
source: Nef Glu160 of the motif binds to basic residues on both σ2 and α (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure, shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Nef Glu154 makes electrostatic interactions with a second basic patch on σ2.
source: Residues of H4, notably Glu154, make electrostatic interactions with a second basic patch on σ2 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure, shown in Figure 3C.

claim: H4 and the dileucine motif have little or no interaction with the Nef core.
source: H4 and the dileucine motif have little or no interaction with the Nef core, and their conformation seems to be specified by their interactions with α–σ2.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: The conformation of H4 and the dileucine motif seems to be specified by their interactions with α–σ2.
source: H4 and the dileucine motif have little or no interaction with the Nef core, and their conformation seems to be specified by their interactions with α–σ2.
evidence: This is an inference from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: Helix H5 and the C-terminal turn segment of the Nef loop are sandwiched between α–σ2 and the Nef core.
source: In contrast, helix H5 and the C-terminal turn segment are sandwiched between α–σ2 and the Nef core.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: The structure of helix H5 and the C-terminal turn segment clearly depends on the interactions with α–σ2.
source: Their structure clearly depends on the interactions with α–σ2, since they are not otherwise visualized in this conformation.
evidence: This is an inference from the crystal structure analysis and comparison to other structures.

claim: The Nef core has an important role in organizing the H5 and C-terminal turn segment.
source: However, the Nef core also seems to have an important role in organizing this segment.
evidence: This is an inference from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: H5 packs against the β-sheet of the Nef core.
source: H5 packs against the β-sheet of the core, and serves primarily to orient the hydrophobic loop with respect to the dileucine motif.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: H5 serves primarily to orient the hydrophobic loop with respect to the dileucine motif.
source: H5 packs against the β-sheet of the core, and serves primarily to orient the hydrophobic loop with respect to the dileucine motif.
evidence: This is an inference from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: The tight turns of the C-terminal part of the Nef loop serve to project a number of charged and hydrophobic side chains into complementary interactions with both α and σ2.
source: The tight turns of the C-terminal part of the loop serve to project a number of charged and hydrophobic side chains into complementary interactions with both α and σ2 (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure, shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The turn-rich section of the Nef loop from 171–179 is anchored at its ends by H5 and by the strand β5 of the core.
source: This unusual sequence of turns is anchored at its ends by H5 and by the strand β5 of the core.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: The turn-rich section of the Nef loop from 171–179 is anchored internally by a hydrogen bond between Nef Asp174 and the main-chain amide of Gln104.
source: The whole turn-rich section of the loop from 171–179 is anchored internally by a hydrogen bond between Nef Asp174 and the main-chain amide of Gln104, and by a partially buried salt bridge between Nef Asp175 of the loop and Nef Arg134 of the core β sheet (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure, shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The turn-rich section of the Nef loop from 171–179 is anchored internally by a partially buried salt bridge between Nef Asp175 of the loop and Nef Arg134 of the core β sheet.
source: The whole turn-rich section of the loop from 171–179 is anchored internally by a hydrogen bond between Nef Asp174 and the main-chain amide of Gln104, and by a partially buried salt bridge between Nef Asp175 of the loop and Nef Arg134 of the core β sheet (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure, shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Residues of Nef helix H3 of the core directly contact AP-2.
source: The structure also reveals that residues of Nef helix H3 of the core directly contact AP-2.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: Nef Gln104, Arg105, and Asp108 bind to a basic patch on α.
source: In particular, Gln104, Arg105, and Asp108 bind to a basic patch on α (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure, shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Nef Pro129 of the β2-β3 loop forms van der Waals interactions with atoms of the α Arg341 side-chain.
source: There is one other minor interaction with the core region, involving Nef Pro129 of the β2-β3 loop. The Pro side-chain forms van der Waals interactions with atoms of the α Arg341 side-chain.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: AP-2 σ2 Y62A and A63D mutations eliminated binding to Nef.
source: Mutations in the regions of AP-2 that were already known to bind dileucine signals had the expected loss of interaction. These include σ2 Y62A and A63D (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a finding from Y3H experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: AP-2 σ2 R60E mutation eliminated binding to Nef.
source: Mutations in regions unique to Nef binding, notably σ2 R60E (Figure 5C) and α E342K (Figure 5D), also eliminated binding.
evidence: This is a finding from Y3H experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: AP-2 α E342K mutation eliminated binding to Nef.
source: Mutations in regions unique to Nef binding, notably σ2 R60E (Figure 5C) and α E342K (Figure 5D), also eliminated binding.
evidence: This is a finding from Y3H experiments shown in Figure 5D.

claim: AP-2 σ2 N48A, H85A, and C99A and α V300A, Q301A, and N344A mutations had lesser mutational phenotypes, if any.
source: Other nearby residues with more peripheral interactions, including σ2 N48A, H85A, and C99A and α V300A, Q301A, and N344A, had lesser mutational phenotypes, if any (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is a finding from Y3H experiments shown in Figures 5C and 5D.

claim: The Nef mutant Q104A behaves like wild type in both binding to α–σ2 and CD4 downregulation.
source: The Nef mutant Q104A behaves like wild type in both binding to α–σ2 (Figure 5B) and CD4 downregulation (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is a finding from Y3H and FACS experiments shown in Figures 5B and 6A,B.

claim: The Nef charge-reversal mutant D108K eliminates α–σ2 binding as judged by Y3H.
source: The charge-reversal mutant D108K, however, eliminates α–σ2 binding as judged by Y3H (Figure 5B) and CD4 downregulation (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is a finding from Y3H experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The Nef charge-reversal mutant D108K eliminates CD4 downregulation.
source: The charge-reversal mutant D108K, however, eliminates α–σ2 binding as judged by Y3H (Figure 5B) and CD4 downregulation (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is a finding from FACS experiments shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: The Nef D108K mutation is consistent with the salt bridge seen between α Lys299 and Nef Asp108 in the structure.
source: This finding is consistent with the salt bridge seen between α Lys299 and Nef Asp108 in the structure.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the mutational data to the structural data.

claim: Nef Pro129 mutation has no effect on the interaction with AP-2.
source: Another core residue, Pro129, has limited van der Waals interactions with α, thus it was not surprising that its mutation has no effect on the interaction (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from Y3H experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The structure of the AP-2:Nef complex places Nef proximal to the membrane such that the N-terminal helix H1 is aligned parallel and in contact with the membrane.
source: The consensus docking of the AP-2:Nef complex places Nef proximal to the membrane such that the N-terminal helix H1 is aligned parallel and in contact with the membrane (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: This is a finding from the structural model shown in Figures 7A and 7B.

claim: The C-terminus of helix H2 and parts of the central loop of Nef align such that they would contact the membrane surface.
source: The C-terminus of helix H2 and parts of the central loop also align such that they would contact the membrane surface.
evidence: This is a finding from the structural model.

claim: The N-terminus of H1 is exposed to solvent such that there would be nothing to impede contact of the myristoylated N-terminus with the membrane.
source: The N-terminus of H1 is exposed to solvent such that there would be nothing to impede contact of the myristoylated N-terminus with the membrane.
evidence: This is a finding from the structural model.

claim: The exposed face of H1 conjoins with H2 and parts of the central loop of Nef and the membrane-proximal parts of AP-2 to form a bowl that is 30 × 30 Å across, with a clearance of ∼10 Å from the membrane.
source: Indeed, the exposed face of H1 conjoins with H2 and parts of the central loop of Nef and the membrane-proximal parts of AP-2 to form a bowl that is 30 × 30 Å across, with a clearance of ∼10 Å from the membrane (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a finding from the structural model shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The exposed face of H1 contains residues Trp57 and Leu58 that have been implicated in direct binding to CD4.
source: Strikingly, the exposed face of H1 contains residues Trp57 and Leu58 that have been implicated in direct binding to CD4 (Grzesiek et al., 1996a; Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a finding from the structural model shown in Figure 7D, supported by citation to Grzesiek et al., 1996a.

claim: Nef residues Leu97, Arg106, and Leu110 project into the bowl formed by the AP-2:Nef complex.
source: Other residues implicated in CD4 binding, including Leu97, Arg106, and Leu110, also project into the bowl (Grzesiek et al., 1996a).
evidence: This is a finding from the structural model, supported by citation to Grzesiek et al., 1996a.

claim: Multivalent interactions between Nef, CD4, and AP-2 likely drive cooperativity in the formation of the ternary complex.
source: This suggests that multivalent interactions between Nef, CD4, and AP-2 likely drive cooperativity in the formation of the ternary complex.
evidence: This is an inference from the structural model.

claim: The structure of the AP-2:Nef complex provides a framework to unify nearly two decades' worth of research of the molecular basis for CD4 downregulation by Nef.
source: The structure of the AP-2:Nef complex provides a framework to unify nearly two decades' worth of research of the molecular basis for CD4 downregulation by Nef.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the significance of the findings.

claim: The large majority of Nef residues that have been implicated in CD4 downregulation reside in the central loop.
source: The large majority of Nef residues that have been implicated in CD4 downregulation reside in the central loop.
evidence: This is a summary of previous research findings.

claim: All of the Nef central loop residues implicated in CD4 downregulation are well ordered in the complex.
source: The structure shows that all of these residues are well ordered in the complex, in contrast to all previous structures of Nef–effector complexes.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: Nearly all of the Nef central loop residues implicated in CD4 downregulation directly contact AP-2.
source: Nearly all of these Nef residues directly contact AP-2.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: Asp175 had been anticipated to bind to a basic patch on the surface of the α subunit.
source: One notable exception is Asp175, which had been anticipated to bind to a basic patch on the surface of the α subunit.
evidence: This is a statement about previous expectations.

claim: The structure revealed an unexpected role for Asp175 in stabilizing the conformation of the central loop.
source: The structure revealed an unexpected role for Asp175 in stabilizing the conformation of the central loop.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: The Nef core has both a direct role in forming polar interactions with AP-2 and an indirect role in scaffolding the conformation of the central loop.
source: The structure also shows that the Nef core has both a direct role in forming polar interactions with AP-2 and an indirect role in scaffolding the conformation of the central loop.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: The role of Asp174 and Asp175 amounts to the formation of an effector-specific polar core within Nef.
source: The role of Asp174 and Asp175 amounts to the formation of an effector-specific polar core within Nef.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural findings.

claim: The unusual architecture of Nef, as a single domain protein with disproportionately large internal loops, gives Nef an exceptional degree of plasticity, allowing multiple functions to be encoded within a relatively small structure.
source: This provides insight into the underlying reason for the unusual architecture of Nef, as a single domain protein with disproportionately large internal loops. This architecture gives Nef an exceptional degree of plasticity, allowing multiple functions to be encoded within a relatively small structure.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural findings.

claim: The structure is consistent with the emerging consensus picture that all activated AP complexes seem to bind to membranes in the same conformation and the same geometry.
source: The structure is beautifully consistent with the emerging consensus picture that all activated AP complexes seem to bind to membranes in the same conformation and the same geometry (Jackson et al., 2010; Canagarajah et al., 2013; Ren et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural findings, supported by citations to Jackson et al., 2010; Canagarajah et al., 2013; Ren et al., 2013.

claim: The membrane-docking geometry suggested by the unlocked states of AP-1 and AP-2 places Nef such that it is touching the membrane, with its N-terminal region membrane proximal.
source: The membrane-docking geometry suggested by the unlocked states of AP-1 and AP-2 places Nef such that it is touching the membrane, with its N-terminal region membrane proximal.
evidence: This is an inference from the structural model.

claim: The membrane-docking geometry is consistent with Nef's essential N-terminal myristoylation.
source: This is consistent with its essential N-terminal myristoylation.
evidence: This is an inference from the structural model.

claim: The first helix of the β2-adaptin trunk collides sterically with Nef in the modeled conformation.
source: One question still to be resolved is the disposition of the first helix of the β2-adaptin trunk, which collides sterically with Nef in the modeled conformation.
evidence: This is a finding from the structural model.

claim: The first helix of the β2-adaptin trunk could pivot out of the way to avoid steric collision with Nef.
source: It seems straightforward that this helix could pivot out of the way, but this has yet to be directly tested.
evidence: This is a speculation about how the steric collision could be resolved.

claim: The general proximity of Nef, and its N-terminal region in particular, to the membrane is similar to the model proposed for the AP-1:Nef complex that functions in MHC-I downregulation.
source: The general proximity of Nef, and its N-terminal region in particular, to the membrane is similar to the model proposed for the AP-1:Nef complex that functions in MHC-I downregulation (Jia et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison to a previous model, supported by citation to Jia et al., 2012.

claim: The details of the molecular contacts between Nef and the membrane surface differ between the AP-2:Nef and AP-1:Nef complexes.
source: However, the details of the molecular contacts between Nef and the membrane surface differ (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a finding from comparison of the structural models, shown in Figure 8.

claim: Nef has more than one way to interact with membrane surfaces.
source: This suggests that Nef has more than one way to interact with membrane surfaces.
evidence: This is an inference from the comparison of the AP-2:Nef and AP-1:Nef structural models.

claim: Residues of Nef helices H1 and H3 that are implicated in CD4 binding form one edge of a cavern 10 Å high and 30 × 30 Å across, with the membrane serving as the floor.
source: Residues of Nef helices H1 and H3 that are implicated in CD4 binding form one edge of a cavern 10 Å high and 30 × 30 Å across, with the membrane serving as the floor.
evidence: This is a finding from the structural model.

claim: The Nef binding site on CD4 comprises an approximate 17-residue tract that begins ∼10 residues C-terminal to the end of the transmembrane helix.
source: The Nef binding site on CD4 comprises an approximate 17-residue tract (Preusser et al., 2001) that begins ∼10 residues C-terminal to the end of the transmembrane helix.
evidence: Supported by citation to Preusser et al., 2001.

claim: The entirety of the cavern formed by the AP-2:Nef complex is within 10 Å of the membrane surface.
source: The entirety of the cavern is within 10 Å of the membrane surface.
evidence: This is a finding from the structural model.

claim: Localization of the CD4 tail within the cavern would be completely consistent with the proximity of the Nef binding site and transmembrane domain of CD4.
source: Thus localization of the CD4 tail within the cavern would be completely consistent with the proximity of the Nef binding site and transmembrane domain of CD4.
evidence: This is an inference from the structural model.

claim: The N-terminal loop of Nef is required for high-affinity binding to the CD4 cytosolic tail.
source: The N-terminal loop of Nef is required for high-affinity binding to the CD4 cytosolic tail (Preusser et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citation to Preusser et al., 2001.

claim: The N-terminal loop of Nef folds around the CD4 tail within or at the edge of the cavern.
source: We therefore propose that the N-terminal loop of Nef folds around the CD4 tail within or at the edge of the cavern.
evidence: This is a proposal based on the structural model and previous findings.

claim: The dissociation constants for CD4:Nef and AP-2:Nef are both approximately 1 μM.
source: The dissociation constants for CD4:Nef and AP-2:Nef are known separately, and both are approximately 1 μM.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: The affinity and kinetics of CD4 binding to the AP-2:Nef complex are unknown.
source: The affinity and kinetics of CD4 binding to the AP-2:Nef complex are unknown, but this model suggests that the binding would likely be tighter than for these isolated components, and the off rate correspondingly slower.
evidence: This is a statement about the lack of knowledge.

claim: The binding of CD4 to the AP-2:Nef complex would likely be tighter than for the isolated components, and the off rate correspondingly slower.
source: The affinity and kinetics of CD4 binding to the AP-2:Nef complex are unknown, but this model suggests that the binding would likely be tighter than for these isolated components, and the off rate correspondingly slower.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the structural model.

claim: Tighter binding of CD4 to the AP-2:Nef complex would contribute to delivery of CD4 to the ESCRT machinery and its ultimate degradation in the lysosome.
source: This would contribute to delivery of CD4 to the ESCRT machinery and its ultimate degradation in the lysosome (daSilva et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural model, supported by citation to daSilva et al., 2009.

claim: The search for ways to combat the emergence of resistance to antiretrovirals, and to ultimately eradicate HIV, has led to an intense interest in targeting the interactions of HIV and host proteins.
source: The search for ways to combat the emergence of resistance to antiretrovirals, and to ultimately eradicate HIV, has led to an intense interest in targeting the interactions of HIV and host proteins (Jaeger et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Jaeger et al., 2011.

claim: The ideal host protein target site would be essential for the viral replication cycle, yet dispensable for host function.
source: The ideal host protein target site would be essential for the viral replication cycle, yet dispensable for host function.
evidence: This is a statement about the criteria for an ideal drug target.

claim: The ideal host protein target site would be highly invaginated and capable of binding small molecules.
source: Such a site would also be 'groovy', that is to say, highly invaginated and capable of binding small molecules.
evidence: This is a statement about the criteria for an ideal drug target.

claim: The interaction surface complementary to the C-terminal turn segment of the Nef central loop would appear to fit the criterion for an ideal drug target.
source: The interaction surface complementary to the C-terminal turn segment of the Nef central loop would appear to fit this criterion.
evidence: This is a speculation about the potential for drug targeting based on the structural findings.

claim: A deep pocket in AP-2 directly below the binding site for Nef Arg178 appears to be under-utilized by Nef.
source: Indeed, a deep pocket in AP-2 directly below the binding site for Nef Arg178 appears to be under-utilized by Nef (Figure 9).
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure, shown in Figure 9.

claim: Future analysis of the ternary AP-2:Nef:CD4 tail complex may reveal additional promising sites for drug targeting.
source: Future analysis of the ternary AP-2:Nef:CD4 tail complex may reveal additional promising sites.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research directions.

claim: Nef Glu177 is the primary interaction partner for α Arg341.
source: The present structure revealed that Nef Glu177 is the primary interaction partner for α Arg341.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: The Nef E177K mutant manifested a reduction in both α–σ2 binding and CD4 downregulation.
source: The Nef E177K mutant manifested a reduction in both α–σ2 binding (Figure 5B) and CD4 downregulation (Figure 6A,B), consistent with its structural role.
evidence: This is a finding from Y3H and FACS experiments shown in Figures 5B and 6A,B.

claim: The basic patch on α is better conceived of as a polar, rather than basic, patch.
source: The deepened insight obtained from the crystal structure shows that this patch is better conceived of as a polar, rather than basic, patch.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural findings.

claim: The side chain of α Glu342 has a close approach to Nef Arg178.
source: For example, the side chain of α Glu342 has a close approach to Nef Arg178.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: Nef Asp174 and Asp175 do not contact AP-2 directly.
source: The finding that Nef Asp174 and Asp175 do not contact AP-2 directly was a surprise.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: Nef Asp174 and Asp175 are required for AP-2 binding.
source: These two residues are required for AP-2 binding (Figure 5B) and CD4 downregulation (Lindwasser et al., 2008), and had been expected to interact with a basic patch on α.
evidence: This is a finding from Y3H experiments shown in Figure 5B, and supported by citation to Lindwasser et al., 2008.

claim: Nef Asp174 and Asp175 are required for CD4 downregulation.
source: These two residues are required for AP-2 binding (Figure 5B) and CD4 downregulation (Lindwasser et al., 2008), and had been expected to interact with a basic patch on α.
evidence: Supported by citation to Lindwasser et al., 2008.

claim: Nef Asp174 is close to the interface with AP-2, but is not in direct contact.
source: They are, in fact, in the general vicinity of a basic patch, close to α Lys298 and Lys299. Nevertheless, Asp174, while close to the interface, is not in direct contact with AP-2.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: The key role of Nef Asp174 is to anchor the turn section to the N-terminus of helix H3.
source: Its key role appears to be to anchor the turn section to the N-terminus of helix H3.
evidence: This is an inference from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: The partial positive charge at the helix N-terminus can form an interaction with Asp side-chains that is almost as energetically favorable as a salt bridge.
source: The partial positive charge at the helix N-terminus can form an interaction with Asp side-chains that is almost as energetically favorable as a salt bridge.
evidence: This is established knowledge about helix-dipole interactions.

claim: Nef Asp174 forms a short hydrogen bond with the main-chain amide group of Nef Gln104.
source: In this case, a short hydrogen bond is formed with the main-chain amide group of Nef Gln104.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: Nef Asp175 has a similar role in conformational stabilization as Asp174.
source: Asp175 has a similar role in conformational stabilization.
evidence: This is an inference from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: Nef Asp175 is partially buried in a contact with the Nef core, and forms a salt bridge with Arg134.
source: Asp175 is partially buried in a contact with the Nef core, and forms a salt bridge with Arg134.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: The internal Nef Arg134-Asp175 salt bridge is important for stabilizing the C-terminal turn portion of the central loop in its AP-2 binding conformation.
source: We hypothesized that the internal Nef Arg134-Asp175 internal salt bridge is important for stabilizing the C-terminal turn portion of the central loop in its AP-2 binding conformation.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the crystal structure analysis.

claim: Mutation of Nef Arg134 to Glu abrogated interaction of Nef with α–σ2.
source: Indeed, mutation of Arg134 to Glu abrogated interaction of Nef with α–σ2 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from Y3H experiments shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Co-expression in HeLa cells of CD4 with Nef R134E showed that this Nef mutant almost completely lost its ability to downregulate CD4.
source: Moreover, co-expression in HeLa cells of CD4 with Nef R134E followed by FACS analysis showed that this Nef mutant almost completely lost its ability to downregulate CD4 (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is a finding from FACS experiments shown in Figures 6A and 6B.

claim: The Nef R134E mutational phenotype phenocopies the D175A change.
source: These results phenocopy the D175A change (Lindwasser et al., 2008) and are consistent with a critical role for the salt bridge in stabilizing the conformation of the Nef loop required for AP-2 binding and CD4 downregulation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mutational data, supported by citation to Lindwasser et al., 2008.

claim: The Nef R134E and D175A mutational results are consistent with a critical role for the salt bridge in stabilizing the conformation of the Nef loop required for AP-2 binding and CD4 downregulation.
source: These results phenocopy the D175A change (Lindwasser et al., 2008) and are consistent with a critical role for the salt bridge in stabilizing the conformation of the Nef loop required for AP-2 binding and CD4 downregulation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the mutational data.

claim: One face of Nef helix H3, including residues Gln104 and Asp108, contacts AP-2.
source: While most mutational studies of the Nef-AP-2 interaction focused on the Nef central loop, one face of helix H3, including residues Gln104 and Asp108, contacts AP-2.
evidence: This is a finding from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: A steric clash was observed between Nef and helix 1 of the β2 subunit in the model of the membrane-bound AP-2:Nef complex.
source: A steric clash was observed with helix 1 of the β2 subunit.
evidence: This is a finding from the structural model.

claim: β2 helix 1 was previously shown to be conformationally labile in the unlatching (partial activation) of AP-2.
source: β2 helix 1 was previously shown to be conformationally labile in the unlatching (partial activation) of AP-2 (Kelly et al., 2008), and it seems reasonable to expect that it pivots in the full AP-2:Nef complex to prevent a collision.
evidence: Supported by citation to Kelly et al., 2008.

claim: It seems reasonable to expect that β2 helix 1 pivots in the full AP-2:Nef complex to prevent a collision with Nef.
source: β2 helix 1 was previously shown to be conformationally labile in the unlatching (partial activation) of AP-2 (Kelly et al., 2008), and it seems reasonable to expect that it pivots in the full AP-2:Nef complex to prevent a collision.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the structural model and previous findings.
